sentences: Credit utilization is by far the most important driver of default risk, accounting for about 27% of the model's importance, and risk rises steadily as utilization increases, with the strongest effect at the highest levels.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, with a moderate to strong effect, and default risk jumps once an applicant has at least one delinquency.
The effect of utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies, so high utilization matters much more for applicants who have had several delinquencies.
Income and the length of credit history are both moderate drivers, ranking third or fourth, and default risk decreases as income and credit history length rise.
The debt-to-income ratio is a weak to moderate driver ranked fifth, with risk increasing as the ratio rises.

The number of recent inquiries has at most a weak effect, and age and months at the current address hardly matter, while the number of dependents has at most a weak effect. The data do not settle whether credit history length and recent inquiries interact.
Credit utilization and income, and credit utilization and credit history length, do not interact in any meaningful way.
